Decided with GTR 2026-10-03: 'Use CIII].'

The catalogue 0.1633 is a SINGLE entry in NED's 45 (2022ApJS..261...30M); the modal published value is 0.164 with 28 entries, +180 km/s, with a further cluster of 5 at 0.1643 and 3 at 0.165. NED reports NO method or spectral feature for any of the 45 -- every one is flagged 'uncertain origin' -- so this is the published consensus, not a narrow-line measurement, and the 28 may descend from one source as the 75 entries at 0.100 did for PG 0804+761. Adopted on the published record alone and NOT on the UV lines: 0.1643 (+258) would sit closer to the C III] cross-correlation's +270, and choosing it for that reason is exactly what the rule at index 111 forbids. The internal anchors do agree in direction -- at 0.1633 both C III] (+270, S/N 11) and Mg II (+660, S/N 8) say the model sits blueward of the data -- but the C III] blend's three band ratios barely move across a +/-600 km/s scan (1.03-1.05 throughout), so the UV spectrum cannot locate the frame itself. CAUTION: the C IV blueshift is not a smooth function of the frame here -- 128.4 at 0.1633, 266.5 at +100 km/s, then 611.4 at +200 -- so the half-flux point crosses a feature between those steps and the measurement is unusually redshift-sensitive. Proposed with GTR 2026-10-07. ADOPTED by GTR 2026-10-07 after comparing the refits: 'iter06_z164_low is the best fit, manmask=2'. What +180 km/s bought, measured on the adopted fit: residuals improve slightly (C IV 0.79 -> 0.74, C III] 1.02 -> 1.00, Mg II 1.05 -> 1.02 sigma rms) and the anchors move only part of the way -- C III] +270 -> +300 and Mg II +660 -> +630 on low, +270 -> +140 and +660 -> +490 on mod. Closing them would need +600 km/s or more, past every published value, and is not done: the residual offset is the object's own UV blueshift, as at index 111. The change also makes the measurement MORE basis-sensitive, not less -- at 0.1633 low and mod differ by three quanta (335.5 against 128.4), at 0.164 by five (611.4 against 335.5) -- which is why index 112 carries manmask 2.
